title: Custodial key-usage anomaly aggregator and retention snapshot packager
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a pipeline that correlates custodial KMS/HSM key usage events with rotation windows and retention policies to produce tamper-evident retention snapshots and anomaly summaries for audit requests. The feature targets customers using Redwood Private and Dedicated who need per-tenant legal retention exports that include signed manifests, event provenance, and anomaly annotations useful for compliance reviews and incident investigations.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests KMS/HSM key events (encrypt/decrypt, wrap/unwrap, rotate, grant/revoke) from primary sources (Cloud KMS audit logs, HSM syslog, internal key-service event bus) and normalizes into a canonical schema

Retention snapshot export packages include: signed manifest (sha256), per-key usage timeline, rotation events, list of active wrapping keys, and policy metadata; packages are stored in S3 with immutable object lock for 180 days
Automated anomaly detector flags spikes in cross-region decryption or unauthorized wrapping key use; flagged anomalies included in the export with severity level and suggested follow-ups
Exports are verifiable by an external auditor using a signed root attestation key and include provenance chains back to KMS/HSM events
End-to-end test harness simulating cross-region rotation and a simulated HSM emergency rotation; evidence package generated and verified in CI
Ops runbook and dashboard tile in Console showing pipeline health, export queue depth, and recent anomalies
design_notes: We reuse the canonical event schema created for ENG-31402 but add additional canonical fields for wrapping_key_id, wrapping_key_provider (AWS_KMS|GCP_KMS|HSM), operation_type, and rotation_window_id. To ensure non-repudiation, each package will carry signatures from two independent roots: a signing key from the key-service (ephemeral) and a long-lived attestation key stored in HSM and rotated quarterly. Trade-offs: signing every intermediate event is costlier and increases storage; instead we sign package manifests and retain a hashed Merkle root of event batches for compact tamper evidence. For storage immutability we will use S3 Object Lock + Glacier Vault Lock for longer-term archives. Privacy: per-tenant exports must scrub unrelated tenant identifiers; our exporter will run per-tenant job sandboxed in the Private control plane.
implementation_updates: 2025-11-12: Spike complete - ingested sample CloudTrail + HSM syslog into canonical schema. Parser for PKCS#11 logs needs normalization mapping (in progress).
2025-11-15: Prototype manifest format v0.1 landed in git: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-evidence/pull/189. PR has initial JSON schema for manifest and Merkle root calculation.

2025-11-18: Anomaly heuristics defined: cross-region decryption rate > 3x baseline for 10 minutes, wrapping key changes outside maintenance window, and unknown principal access. Implemented basic detector lambda and integrated with alerting.
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag for Redwood Private customers in EU region. Phase 1: internal exports for compliance team (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta for 3 customers with legal-readiness (4 weeks). Phase 3: general availability with SLA for export turnaround (60 minutes) and documented API. Rollback: disable exporter and mark pending jobs as failed with a signed tombstone artifact.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard tile showing last successful export per tenant, queue depth, processing latency percentile (p50/p95/p99). Alerts: export-failure-rate > 1% in 15m, detector-error-rate > 0.5% in 5m, manifest-signing-failure. Pager rotation includes oncall-sre and compliance-eng.
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization, integration tests ingesting synthetic KMS + HSM events (PKCS#11), CI job that runs a simulated emergency rotation and verifies package signature with attestation key, fuzz tests for large event windows, and performance tests to validate throughput targets (10k key events/hour per region).
